title: Signal-fusion token gating and latency-sag restoration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: reduce p99 tail latency and smoothing latency sag under bursty, heterogeneous workloads by combining a lightweight multi-signal admission gate with virtualized slot weighting and a soft time-slicing prefill strategy. Scope covers admission policy, token-weight decay heuristics, runtime kernel swap triggers, and decode time-slice orchestration for long sequences.

Background: current continuous-batching pipeline handles varying sequence lengths well on average, but we see recurring p99 spikes when short-latency requests collide with a handful of long-decode requests and when kernel selection is suboptimal under transient load. Existing approaches (strict reservation, hard preemption) are either too wasteful or cause throughput collapse. We need a middle-ground that: (1) detects imminent latency sag from fused signals, (2) gracefully reduces head-of-line blocking without starving throughput, and (3) keeps model quality degradation minimal when falling back to faster kernels.

Design overview:
1) Signal fusion admission gate: build a compact aggregator of three signals per serving node: incoming short-window token arrival rate, current KV cache hit fraction, and per-kernel decode backlog estimate. We compute a single admission score (0..1) using an exponentially-weighted blend; high score => allow immediate admission, low score => go to virtual slot queue.
2) Virtual slot weighting with token-decay: instead of reserving physical slots, requests pushed to the virtual queue receive a decaying token-weight that reduces their admission priority over time (so long-running requests don't monopolize slots). We implement token-weight decay as integer counters per request bucket to keep memory use tiny.
3) Soft time-slicing for decode: for sequences above length threshold (configurable by model), we allow the decoder to yield after a short time-slice (e.g., 40ms), returning an intermediate chunk to the admission layer which can interleave shorter requests. This reduces head-of-line blocking while preserving autoregressive correctness by resuming the same KV context.
4) Kernel-swap fallback: when admission score is low and a request is latency-sensitive (marked by client hint or small max_tokens), consider switching to a lower-precision kernel path (quantized int8 kernel) mid-decode. Kernel swap is allowed only if model-compatibility table marks the model safe and a brief quality degradation check passes (historical delta below threshold).

Telemetry and SLOs: instrument p50/p95/p99, 95th decode-chunk duration, admission queue length, kernel-swap frequency, and quality delta for swapped requests. Target: reduce p99 by >=20% on bursty workloads, keep p50 within 5% of baseline, and keep kernel-swap quality delta under defined threshold.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: introducing signal fusion and virtual slot counters adds state to the serving nodes. We keep that state bounded and sharded per worker to limit memory.
- Quality: kernel-swap can affect output; conservative gating and Canary evaluation required.
- Debuggability: time-slicing increases partial-output artifacts (intermediate outputs) which need tracing to reconstruct end-to-end output for audits.

Testing plan: microbenchmarks with synthetic mixes (short-only, long-only, mixed bursts) using our perf harness; staging tests on dedicated pool with production traffic replay for 48h; A/B canary with 5% of hosts for 24h observing tail latencies and quality.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated at node-level. Phase 1: enable admission gate + virtual slots (no kernel-swap, no time-slicing) on staging. Phase 2: add soft time-slicing and monitor invariants. Phase 3: enable conservative kernel-swap for compatible models behind an opt-in client header. Gradual canary 5/20/50/100.

Acceptance criteria:
- Staging p99 improvement >= 15% on mixed workloads without throughput regression.
- No more than 0.5% of requests see kernel-swap quality delta above threshold.
- Observability dashboards created and annotated with expected baselines.
